request.idea: Every clock in the world suddenly stops except one.

bible.title: The Last Tick
bible.userIdea: Every clock in the world suddenly stops except one.
bible.premise: A silver thread links every clock in the world, carrying their movement between them. When the thread catches around a winding key, the network stops, except for one clock protected by a loose loop.
bible.hook: Why does one clock keep ticking when all the others have fallen silent?
bible.goal: Discover why the last clock still ticks and restore the silent clocks without losing its movement.
bible.centralProblem: The children must understand how a tangled silver thread has stopped the connected clocks before their repairs silence the remaining one.
bible.stakes: Their only working guide to the mystery could stop before they understand what makes it different.
bible.motif: A silver loop that opens and closes with each tick.

sentences.text: Across the clockwork gallery's world-clock display, not one hand moved.
Tick, tick—the glass-sided clock kept going.
Ravi bent towards its winding key; Leo checked the display again while Mina peered beside the swinging pendulum.
"What has this one got that the others haven't?" Leo asked.

sentences.text: Mina followed a silver thread from the silent display to the winding key.
It curled around the key, leaving one loose loop beside the pendulum.
She crouched lower: the loop stirred with each swing, but the branching thread stayed still.
"There," she said, and the others bent beside her.

sentences.text: "Turn it back," Mina said. "That loose loop let this pendulum swing when the others couldn't."
Ravi reversed the key while Leo lifted the thread clear of the pendulum.
The last curl slipped off the stem, and the glass clock ticked again.
Movement ran through the silver branches; across the whole display, every clock's hands began to move.
